question: Many young people today spend too much time following the latest fashion trends in areas such as clothing and technology. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

In conclusion, I believe that following fashion and technology trends offers valuable opportunities for today’s youth. It not only encourages creativity but also opens doors to careers in the growing digital and creative industries.

In conclusion, while it is true that economic progress plays an integral role in the development of a country, it is my firm belief that the increase in quality of life of people is a country’s fundamental goal.

question: Topic: The increase in the production of consumer goods results in damage to the natural environment. What are the causes of this? What can be done to solve this problem?

The damage to the natural environment increased alongside with the growth of consumer goods production. Product packaging wastes and the unprocessed chemical materials involved in production processes are the main key factors why this issue happened. Government involvement is crucial in solving this issue by establishing sets of regulations to govern the consumer goods industry.

The production of consumer products ruins the environment due to two main reasons, namely unrecyclable packaging and the involvement of multiple chemical products throughout the manufacturing processes. Hard-to-recycle packaging, such as cans from soda products, will end up in a landfill up to a hundred years before it dissolves. Tons of canned waste will damage the soil as well as the air around the landfill. Furthermore, several chemical materials utilized during the production are not well managed and neutralized. Usually, these chemical wastes will be thrown directly into the river, thus impacting the water quality.

The government plays an important role in solving this issue. Sets of regulations can be established to govern the consumer goods industry, starting from raw material preparation to waste management. For instance, national authorities can set the standard on the type of waste and percentage of remaining particular chemicals that are allowed to be dumped into the environment, such as limiting the percentage of PET to around 3% in the waste. Water pollution can be highly suppressed if these regulations are successfully applied to all consumer product manufacturers.

Rapidly increased consumer goods production impacts the stability of nature, mainly due to the recyclable packaging and unneutralized chemical products involved in the production processes. I believe that the government should implement sets of regulations to solve this issue.

On one hand, those who claim that history has limited relevance today often argue that the world has transformed drastically over time. They assert that the historical context, technology, and socio-political landscape are significantly different from the present, making it challenging to draw direct parallels. For instance, the complexities of global interconnectivity, the digital revolution, and the intricate geopolitical dynamics of today appear to be uncharted territories in the historical record.

Furthermore, skeptics argue that history can be selective and biased, reflecting the perspectives of those in power. This, they contend, can distort our understanding of past events, potentially leading to misconceptions about their relevance to current issues.

However, proponents of the idea that history is crucial for understanding the present emphasize the value of historical patterns and lessons. They posit that underlying human behaviors and societal patterns have remained consistent throughout history, offering insights into how societies have evolved, grappled with challenges, and learned from past mistakes.

In my view, history is undeniably relevant in the present day. While the specifics of certain events may differ, the fundamental aspects of human behavior, decision-making, and the consequences of actions have retained their universality. By studying history, we can identify recurring themes, learn from past errors, and draw on the wisdom of our ancestors to navigate contemporary challenges.

In conclusion, the value of history in the modern world is a subject of debate. While some argue that history offers limited insight into current issues, I firmly believe that the study of the past is indispensable for comprehending and addressing present-day challenges. History provides us with a broader perspective and a wealth of lessons that can inform our approach to contemporary issues.

There are certainly insights to be gained from studying past conflicts, but they will rarely result in fixed, black and white rules apply to every new situation.

In conclusion, antiquity is not a simple road map for the future. Those who are too avid to accept seemingly apparent lessons are doomed to lead themselves astray and make new mistakes.

question: There are severe social consequences to housing shortages in cities, and only the government can solve these problems. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Housing shortages in cities lead to serious social consequences, such as increased homelessness, overcrowding, and rising property prices. One of the major social consequences of housing shortages is homelessness. This issue can contribute to higher crime rates, mental health problems, and social unrest. Additionally, overcrowding in cities forces many people to live in substandard conditions, which negatively affects their well-being and quality of life. The rising cost of housing also creates economic inequality, as lower-income groups struggle to afford decent accommodation while wealthier individuals continue to invest in high-priced properties.

The government plays a vital role in tackling these problems by implementing policies that promote affordable housing. By providing subsidies for low-income households, enforcing rent control regulations, and investing in public housing projects, authorities can help mitigate the effects of housing shortages. Furthermore, governments can reform zoning laws and allocate more land for residential use to encourage housing development.

However, relying solely on government intervention may not be sufficient. Private sector participation is essential to increasing the supply of affordable homes. Governments should incentivize private developers to build cost-effective housing through tax breaks, reduced bureaucracy, and public-private partnerships. Non-governmental organizations and community-driven initiatives can also contribute by supporting housing projects for disadvantaged groups.

In conclusion, while the government has a significant responsibility in addressing housing shortages, it cannot solve these problems alone. A collaborative effort involving private sector investment, community participation, and policy reforms is essential to ensuring sustainable and affordable housing for urban populations.

In conclusion, although some information—such as trade secrets or national security data—must be protected, I firmly support the notion that most information should be made public. Ultimately, transparency sheds light on complex scientific research and accelerates collective progress.

question: Some people argue that job satisfaction is more important than job security, while others believe that they cannot always expect job satisfaction, and a permanent job is more important. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
essay_text:
People often wrangle over the notion of a perfect job in contemporary society. While some are in favour of a job for life, I believe that job satisfaction lends itself more to the modern labour market as will now be discussed. 

Admittedly, those who argue that job security is an important factor have some solid points. A permanent job gives its holders a sense of security, meaning that no matter how the quality of work, they will wake up the next day safe in the knowledge that they are in a state of employment. This may free them from financial worries and anxiety, because they can rest assured that a constant flow of income will come into their home at the end of the day. The idea of a steady job is therefore attractive to many job seekers, but they should factor in the rapid growth of technology in this digital era. I profoundly believe that the notion of a “safe” job is wrong, given the fact that technology has been replacing innumerable human workers in many industries. 

It is thus more sensible to argue for job fulfilment instead. When an employee does their dream job, they tend to make real efforts to accomplish work rather than waiting for someone else to push them. They are likely to yield higher productivity and willing to learn new things to improve themselves, all of which contribute to their career growth. Those who find their jobs worth doing tend to have the drive to work and advance fast on their career path. A typical example of this is the case story of Bill Gates, who devoted much of his youth to Microsoft and turned it into a behemoth in the IT industry.

In conclusion, the world is always in a constant state of flux. Thus, it is no longer reasonable to hold on a permanent job even if it can give a sense of security to us.
